key_insight: This study will compare multiple large language models against expert human benchmarks for primary care decision support using realistic clinical vignettes in Kenya, Malawi, and Tanzania.
clinical_relevance: It addresses whether LLMs can be safe, contextually appropriate, and clinically sound for low-resource primary healthcare settings in Sub-Saharan Africa.
method: Clinicians will create 200–250 hypothetical patient vignettes per country and write benchmark care plans.
Six open-source and proprietary LLMs will be evaluated in fully crossed repeated-measures comparisons.
Independent experts will rate masked LLM vs human responses on soundness, safety, contextual fit, clarity, and confidence.
evidence_signal: The protocol plans at least 358 evaluations per LLM per country, using expert-adjudicated paired comparisons rather than retrospective chart data.
watch_item: Results may not fully generalize beyond hypothetical vignettes or beyond the specific countries, clinicians, and model set studied.
paper_title: Evaluating large language models as clinical decision support tools in primary healthcare settings: Protocol for a multi-country comparative validation study on expert-adjudicated hypothetical vignettes (hypMOOVE-PHC)
